newsitem.title: BULGARIA: United Bulgarian Bank to increase share capital.
newsitem.headline: United Bulgarian Bank to increase share capital.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-owned United Bulgarian Bank (UBB) decided on Wednesday to raise its capital to 21.07 billion levs from a current 679.5 million levs through a new share issue, a bank executive director said.
"The bank's extraordinary shareholders' meeting decided to raise capital to 21.07 billion levs, revising its previous decision of a capital rise to 16.3 billion levs," Oleg Nedyalkov told reporters.

Shareholders decided on May 31 to increase capital to 16.3 billion levs through a new share issue to be covered mainly by the Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) through domestic bad loan bonds. The BCC manages state equity in local commercial banks.

In June the cabinet distributed $400 million in bad loan bonds issued by the government among seven state-owned banks in a bid to boost their capital to risks assets ratio. The UBB received bonds worth $119 million from the total.

"The additional capital rise to 21 billion levs is due to lev fall against the dollar in past months and also due to the larger than expected volume of bonds received by the bank," a BCC official said.
The BCC, which is a major shareholder in UBB, was expected initially to boost the bank's capital through a transfer of $100 million worth of bad loan bonds.
Bulgaria issued those bonds to cover non-performing loans extended by banks to state enterprises before 1991.
The UBB's gross profit totalled some 20 billion levs at the end of November after a loss of 4.02 billion levs in 1995, preliminary bank figures showed.
The UBB was set up through a merger of 22 smaller institutions four years ago as the first bank consolidation project implemented by the BCC.
Before the capital rise the BCC held 89.2 percent of UBB's capital and now its stake is estimated at more that 98 percent. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
